title: Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index (April 2027), 10:00 a.m. ET
source: EST: the publisher's standing rule, restated on conference-board.org/topics/consumer-confidence fetched direct 2026-09-06 (HTTP 200, 332,031 bytes after one 301) -- "The Conference Board publishes the Consumer Confidence Index (R) at 10 a.m. ET on the last Tuesday of every month." 2027-04-27 is the last Tuesday of April 2027. The rule is verified for APRIL specifically against three primary-sourced April editions fetched direct 2026-09-06, each read at HTTP 200 and confirmed against its own "Source: April <year> Consumer Confidence Survey" line and its "Updated:" date rather than trusted by slug: CCI-Apr-2023 (Updated 2023-04-25), CCI-Apr-2024 (2024-04-30), CCI-Apr-2025 (2025-04-29) -- every one the last Tuesday of its April, and ALL THREE double-sourced by the preceding March edition's own next-release line (CCI-Mar-2023 "The next release is Tuesday, April 25 at 10 AM ET"; CCI-Mar-2024 "Tuesday, April 30th"; CCI-Mar-2025 "Tuesday, April 29th"). CCI-Apr-2021, CCI-Apr-2022 and CCI-Apr-2026 each returned HTTP 200 while serving the current August 2026 edition (332,031 bytes) and are recorded as blocked rather than counted. No April-2027 announcement exists yet, so this is the publisher's rule applied forward against a fully double-sourced April record, not a posted date. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: CANONICAL FILE written by the consumer-confidence-2027-04-27 initial-research lane (2026-09-06) after reading the one prior proposal, proposals/consumer-confidence-2027-04-27.from-consumer-confidence-2027-03-30.json, which is now inert. THE COLLISION INSTANCE of the series: per the Fed's own posted calendar (federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm, fetched 2026-09-06 HTTP 200, 164,831 bytes), 2027-04-27 is FOMC day one of the April 27-28 meeting, one of exactly four colliding 2027 prints (01-26, 04-27, 07-27, 10-26) against eight clean ones. Research finding banked in docs/research/events/consumer-confidence-2027-04-27.md: the collision carries no information channel, for a MECHANICAL reason rather than a statistical one. All 17 CB/FOMC collisions since 2021 are day ONE and none is a decision day -- the Fed's two-day meetings always start on a Tuesday, so a Tuesday release can only ever land on the silent day. The measured Fed effect lives entirely on day two: FOMC decision days run 8 of 9 wider than no-Fed sessions (SPY 1.352/0.958, p=0.0001), while FOMC day ones are 0 of 9 (SPY 0.929/0.958, p=0.2971). Nor has any CB print ever collided with an SEP meeting: 0 of 28 SEP day-ones is the last Tuesday of its month, and the April meeting carries no SEP. April CB days are 0 of 9 against other April sessions AND 0 of 9 against other late-April sessions. The only p<0.05 result anywhere in that session is directional and unregistered -- April CB days run SPY -1.035% close-to-close, 1 of 6 up, p=0.0183 against other late-April sessions -- which is exactly the one hit twelve months of the same test predict by chance at alpha=0.05, does not clear a Bonferroni 0.00417, and is registered as a falsifier rather than a call. Geometry note for whichever lane takes the close-out: sourced April cut-off lags are 6/6/8 days (2023-04-19, 2024-04-24, 2025-04-21), putting a 2027 field window at roughly 04-05 -> 04-20, whose last days sit inside fomc-blackout-start-2027-04-17. Estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
